request_description: For clarity and to assist efficient processing, this request relates to existing corporate governance and equality/human rights duty records. Where any requested record is already publicly available, please provide the direct URL link in lieu of copies. A) Corporate risk management and assurance records 1. Corporate Risk Register (current): The most recent, date-stamped version of the Corporate Risk Register in force as at the date of processing this request. 2. Corporate Risk Register (previous): The immediately preceding date-stamped version (i.e. the version in place before the current one). 3. Directorate / Department risk registers (current): The most recent date-stamped risk register for each Directorate / Department (or equivalent “Level 2” risk registers referenced in governance or audit reporting). 4. Risk controls / mitigations: Where controls or mitigating actions are maintained separately from the risk registers, please provide the current and immediately prior version of those control/mitigation schedules. I am not seeking operational or low-level work instructions. B) Public Sector Equality & Human Rights Duty (Section 42, Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission Act 2014) Having regard to Wicklow County Council’s Public Sector Equality and Human Rights Duty Implementation Plan and related Annual Report disclosures, I request the following records: 6. The Council’s Assessment of Equality and Human Rights Issues completed under Step 1 (Assess) of the Duty (current version). 7. The Evidence Book / evidence records referenced in the Implementation Plan appendices, or equivalent compiled records relied upon by the Section 42 Working Group. 8. The Implementation Template referenced in the Implementation Plan. 9. Governance records relating to the Duty, including: o the terms of reference and membership of the Public Sector Equality and Human Rights Duty Working Group; and o any record confirming approval or adoption of the Implementation Plan by the Senior Management Team (e.g. SMT minutes or decision records). 10. Records relating to training delivered specifically for implementation of the Duty (2024–present), including: • training materials or decks, • training plans, and • attendance records at Senior Management level where recorded. 11. Records relating to the Priority Initiatives identified in the Implementation Plan, limited to: • the review or development of the Staff Charter, Customer Charter, and Customer Service Action Plan insofar as they implement Step 2 (Address); and • internal communications issued to staff regarding the Implementation Plan or Duty implementation. 12. Any monitoring, review, or reporting records prepared to support Step 3 (Report) of the Duty (2024–present), including any internal drafts prepared for inclusion in future Annual Reports.

request_description: I read an article today about the Rainbow Crossing being rejected by Bray MD. I read with great concern some of the comments from Bray Municipal District town engineer Liam Bourke. He is quoted as saying he had "multiple correspondences" from the National Council of the Blind. Under Freedom of Information, could I get a copy of the "multiple correspondences" between the Bray MD Town Engineer and NCBI please? I initiated the rainbow crossing in Arklow. I have had meetings with NCBI and I am also a Disability Activist most of my life, and the Arklow crossing was seen by NCBI who informed me that it would not impact on anyone Blind or Visually impaired as the design is 'outside' of the actual crossing and not part of the crossing. I am waiting for a phone call from NCBI today in relation to this, to clarify what has happened. The Arklow crossing Design does not impact on anyone as stated above, and has been copied by Limerick, Cork, and South County Dublin to name a few. The coloured lines are not part of, or in the pedestrian crossing - training to cross the road at Traffic Lights teaches everyone to walk from kerb to kerb between the solid white lines only - that applies to everyone - the coloured lines are a distance away on the outside of those white lines, so if someone was walking over the coloured lines they do not know how to cross the street. Those that are blind/visually impaired are not taught to cross the street diagonally as it would be dangerous, so they are nowhere near the coloured lines. I have spoken to NCBI about this article, which they now have, and they also have great concerns about being quoted by the Town Engineer as being "opposed" to the crossings, which is not the case. They are looking into this also

request_description: My request relates to successful prosecutions taken by the Authority under the Waste Management Act 1996. Specifically I am looking for the details of all prosecutions taken by the Authority, which resulted in a conviction, fine or penalty, where the case was taken under the following sections of the Act: Section 18 of the Waste Management Act 1996; Section 55 of the Waste Management Act 1996; Section 32 of the Waste Management Act 1996; Section 34 of the Waste Management Act 1996; Section 39 of the Waste Management Act 1996; Section 57/58 of the Waste Management Act 1996. To stay consistent with the information published by the EPA in relation to its enforcement actions I would like to request the following details with respect to each of these cases: Respondent Name; Permit / licence number if applicable; Respondent Address; Section of Waste management Act 1996 that the prosecution was taken under; Case Summary; and The Details of the sentence/ fine/ Costs The information I am seeking is a record of the cases taken and not documents involved in the case itself, it would not form part of the case taken and as such would not be available from the Courts. I understand the information to be available in tabular (spreadsheet) form and has been submitted to the EPA as part of the RMCEI returns process. The information I seek is consistent with the publication of similar information by other prosecuting bodies. For instance, the EPA publishes details of successful prosecutions. The Office of Director of Corporate Enforcment publishes, in its annual report, a table of directors who have been disqualified following court orders. The Revenue Commissioners publishes the list of the tax defaulters, who made settlements in lieu of a court conviction. I do not seek information on parties acquitted or cases where the prosecution did not proceed. Information of this nature is supposed to be public under Article 34 of the Constitution, that justice be administered in public. As such it cannot be considered to be confidential or would ever have the character necessary to be treated as confidential. Under Section 17 of the Act I would ask that the information be released electronically in a .xls or similar file format. If amending the wording of the request is likely to reduce unnecessary workload I am happy to consider an alternative phrasing.
